fieldValues.title: The essay package depends on the argument package for now, and the agent help teaches how to use it
fieldValues.decision_question: How does a new essay get the source, claim and problem types its help and agent brief already assume?
fieldValues.context: Checked 2026-11-04 in srs-web at 8b2fedb: a new essay installs essay 1.8.0 and comments 1.1.0 only. The argument package is not bundled or in packages.lock.json. help/ (essay.links, essay.sources) and the agent handoff (essay-document.ts:642-645) assume its types unconditionally, and adding a source to a new essay throws 'install the argument package' (essay-document.ts:720). Neither the editor nor an agent tool can install a package that is not bundled; package_upgrade needs it already installed. srs-web#590 reported this from the first real use, and muDemocracy.org#303 plans the dependency for essay 1.9.0. installWithDependencies throws on an unmet unbundled dependency, so the bundle must be available first. Owner, vignette 1cfe0647-c01c-4819-964c-97fb8dba4333.
fieldValues.alternatives_considered: A. Leave it and make the help conditional. Leads to: help and code agree, but sources stay broken on a new essay. B. A one-action install in the editor and an agent install tool, argument opt-in. Leads to: new UI, a new engine tool and a step every writer must discover before dragging in a file. C (chosen). Argument as a dependency of essay, bundled with the app. Leads to: new essays work with no step; every essay carries argument definitions, whether or not it needs them. D. A semantic context chosen per essay. Leads to: the likely long-term shape, but far larger; held by the exercise in this commit.
fieldValues.decision_statement: The essay package declares a packageDependency on the argument package (muDemocracy.org#303), srs-web bundles and pins it, and a new essay therefore has source, claim and problem types without an install step. The agent help teaches their use: when to create each, what relates to what, and that the writer decides. This is the interim default, not the model of what an essay's background is.
fieldValues.rationale: C over A because the help's main promise, drag in a source, must work on a new essay. C over B because it needs no new UI or engine tool and leaves the writer nothing to discover; the owner's condition on the argument model was that it be easy to install and explained (vignette 24c38533). C over D because D has open questions and the bug is here now. The owner chose C on 2026-11-04 with the condition that agent help teaches it.
fieldValues.revisit_when: When a kind of writing other than an argued essay, such as a story or contract, is supported, or when argument definitions in every essay prove a cost: size, or concepts that confuse writers who never use them. The exercise on an essay's semantic context supersedes this if it picks another default.
fieldValues.next_steps: muDemocracy.org#303: publish essay 1.9.0 with the dependency and carrying no argument types. srs-web#590: bundle and pin argument, bump essay, teach the agent help and handoff, name the package in a missing-type error for older essays.
